subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Paleomagnetic dating: magnetic polarity reversals used for dating because:
options: Reversals are global, synchronous events recorded in rocks
Reversals are recorded only within a single sedimentary basin
Reversals are not synchronous between different continents
Reversals are local events in the geomagnetic field only
solution: GPTS: Global Polarity Time Scale. Reversals: worldwide. Correlation of magnetozone to GPTS.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Competent vs incompetent layers in folding:
options: Competent layers are thinnest at the fold hinges and thickest on the fold limbs
Competent layers buckle and are thicker at hinges. Incompetent flow into hinges
Both layer types deform identically, so no thickness variation develops anywhere
Incompetent layers remain rigid and unchanged while competent layers thicken on the limbs
solution: Competent: quartzite, sandstone. Incompetent: shale, salt. Parasitic folds in incompetent layers.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which statement about coal ranks is INCORRECT?
options: Anthracite is the highest-rank coal and has the highest carbon content
Peat is the lowest-rank precursor of the coalification sequence
Carbon content increases progressively as rank rises to anthracite
Lignite has a higher carbon content than anthracite
solution: Anthracite, not lignite, has the highest carbon content — the statement is reversed.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer (K = 25 m/day) of cross-section 200 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The groundwater discharge is about:
options: 200 m³/day
5000 m³/day
100 m³/day
50 m³/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the hardness of fluorite on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness?
solution: CaF2. Perfect octahedral cleavage. Fluorescence. Used in optics.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Denudation rate estimation: cosmogenic nuclides (¹⁰Be, ²⁶Al):
options: Lower concentration always indicates a completely stable surface with zero erosion
Concentration shows no relationship to the rate of surface denudation
Accumulation in surface rocks. Higher concentration = slower erosion
Concentration is controlled entirely by the age of the underlying bedrock
solution: ¹⁰Be: production by cosmic rays. Concentration inversely related to denudation rate.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In GIS, which analysis finds the route that minimizes the cumulative cost of movement, weighting distance by factors such as slope?
options: Path minimizing cumulative cost (distance × weight). For pipelines, roads, transmission lines
The path of the shortest straight-line distance between two points, regardless of terrain or land use
A route that minimizes the slope only, while ignoring all land-cover constraints entirely
A path that is selected by the visual interpretation of the topographic map contours
solution: Cost surface: slope, land use, geology, environmental constraints. Dijkstra's algorithm.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following is a recognized type of rock bolt used for ground support?
options: Plain mild-steel rods hammered into the rock without any anchorage and with no grouting at all
Mechanical (expansion shell), Resin-grouted (rebar), Friction (Split set, Swellex)
Only untensioned cement-grouted bars placed in horizontal drill holes
Steel lattice girders wrapped in wire mesh and cast in plain concrete
solution: Rock bolts: tensioned or untensioned. Ground support in tunnels. Pattern or spot bolting.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Igneous rock classification by silica content:
options: Acid >66%, Intermediate 52-66%, Basic 45-52%, Ultrabasic <45% SiO2
On the basis of grain size alone, from coarse phaneritic to aphanitic glassy types
By the modal proportions of quartz, alkali feldspar, plagioclase and feldspathoid
By alkali content only, separating sodic, potassic and calc-alkaline magma series
solution: Granite (acid), Andesite (intermediate), Basalt (basic), Peridotite (ultrabasic).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the age and dominant type of the Deccan Traps volcanic province in India?
options: Granite batholith intruded during the Proterozoic (~2.5 Ga) in the Dharwar craton
Andesite-dominated arc volcanism formed along an ancient subduction zone
Cretaceous-Paleogene (~66 Ma). Flood basalt (continental). 500,000 km²
Rhyolite ignimbrites erupted from a continental rift during the Permian period
solution: Deccan: K-Pg boundary. Reunion hotspot. Intertrappean sedimentary beds.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which sequence correctly lists the stages involved in the formation of sedimentary rocks?
options: Melting → crystallization → cooling → solidification → compaction → cementation
Erosion → melting → compaction → deposition → recrystallization → metamorphism
Deposition → burial → lithification → metamorphism → partial melting → magma crystallization
Weathering → erosion → transport → deposition → compaction → cementation
solution: Lithification: compaction + cementation. Cement: calcite, silica, iron oxide.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In hydrothermal metamorphism, metamorphism is driven primarily by interaction of rocks with:
options: Regional metamorphism at high pressure along convergent plate margins
Dry heating of wall rocks adjacent to a cooling igneous intrusion
Mechanical crushing and grinding of rocks along active fault zones
Hot water-rock interaction. Seafloor (black smokers)
solution: Hydrothermal: mid-ocean ridges. Greenschist facies alteration of basalt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An ore body of 2 Mt has an average metal grade of 2%. The contained metal is about:
options: 4 kt
40 kt
80 kt
20 kt
solution: Metal = tonnage × grade = 2 Mt × 2% = 40 thousand tonnes (kt).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: To extract 5 m³ of coal, 45 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 45/5 = 9 : 1.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The most abundant single mineral group in the crust is:
options: Pyroxene
Feldspar
Amphibole
Olivine
solution: Feldspars make up roughly half of the Earth's crust by volume.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Image processing — atmospheric correction:
options: Remove the geometric distortions caused by satellite roll, pitch and yaw variation of the platform
Remove scattering and absorption effects. Dark object subtraction (DOS), FLAASH, 6S
Convert the DN values to radiance, leaving all of the other atmospheric effects uncorrected
Apply contrast stretching in order to improve the visual appearance of the scenes
solution: Atmospheric: Rayleigh + Mie scattering. Water vapor absorption. DOS: assumes dark pixel = 0 reflectance.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What are the intertrappean beds found between successive basalt flows of the Deccan Traps?
options: Sedimentary layers between basalt flows. Contain fossils (dinosaur eggs, plants)
Igneous sills and dykes that contain no fossils and no sedimentary material at all
Thick coal seams formed in swamps between successive volcanic eruptions in the region
Massive unbroken lava piles without any intervening sedimentary record between flows
solution: Intertrappean: limestone, sandstone, shale. Rajamundry, Jabalpur. Dinosaur eggs at Lameta.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Seismic tomography: 3D velocity model from:
options: First arrival times from a single two layer refraction spread
Dispersion of surface waves recorded along one linear spread
Gravity profile inverted assuming a constant crustal density
Travel time residuals of many ray paths through Earth
solution: Tomography: inverse of many travel times. High velocity = cold/dense. Low velocity = hot/fluid.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) measures:
options: Mass change with temperature
Enthalpy change accompanying thermal events
Electrical conductivity as a function of temperature
Magnetic susceptibility across the heating range
solution: TGA: mass loss = dehydration, decomposition. Steps in curve = distinct reactions.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which processes produce compositionally diverse rocks from a single parent magma?
options: Uniform crystallisation of a melt to yield a single rock type of fixed composition
Processes that produce compositionally diverse rocks from single parent magma
Complete melting of the source rock followed by rapid quench to a glass
Change in magma composition caused only by addition of wall-rock material
solution: Differentiation: fractional crystallization, liquid immiscibility, crystal settling.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The δ¹⁸O value of marine carbonate shells primarily records which parameter of the ambient seawater at the time of precipitation?
options: Salinity alone
Water temperature and isotopic composition of the water
Dissolved oxygen concentration
Only the water depth at the site
solution: δ¹⁸O of biogenic carbonates (foraminifera) varies with both temperature and seawater ¹⁸O composition; this forms the basis of paleotemperature equations and paleoclimate proxies.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which minerals make up the typical mineral composition of a granite?
options: Only quartz and muscovite, with no feldspar or dark ferromagnesian minerals
Only calcic plagioclase and augite, with minor olivine and magnetite
Quartz, calcite, epidote and chlorite typical of greenschist facies rocks
Quartz + K-feldspar + plagioclase + biotite/muscovite
solution: Granite: coarse-grained, felsic. Common in continental crust.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 10 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.01. The Darcy velocity is:
options: 0.1 m/day
0.2 m/day
1000 m/day
10 m/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 30% volatile matter and 10% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+30+10) = 56%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which GIS operation combines two or more raster layers cell-by-cell using arithmetic, comparison or logical functions?
options: Map algebra
Buffer analysis
Vector polygon overlay
Network analysis
solution: Map algebra (raster calculator): cell-by-cell operations across rasters, e.g., weighted sum in landslide susceptibility = slope×0.3 + geology×0.2 + rainfall×0.5.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: According to Davis's cycle of erosion, what is the correct sequence of stages in the denudation chronology of a landscape?
options: A single episode of rapid tectonic uplift is followed immediately by one short burst of vertical river incision
The landscape evolves steadily from old age through maturity and then returns once again to a youthful stage
Youth (high relief, rapid incision) → Maturity (maximum dissection) → Old age (peneplain, low relief)
River erosion and tectonic uplift operate independently of one another showing no sequential development of landforms through time
solution: Davis: time-dependent. Criticized for oversimplifying. Penck's alternative emphasizes uplift rate.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: XRD Bragg's law: nλ = 2d·sin(θ). For Cu Kα (λ=1.54Å), d=3Å, n=1:

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In a reverse or thrust fault, which way does the hanging wall move, and what dip separates a thrust fault from a reverse fault?
options: Hanging wall moves up (compression). Thrust: <45° dip
Hanging wall moves down relative to the footwall under regional extensional stress
Both blocks move horizontally past each other with no vertical component at all
Footwall is displaced upward relative to the hanging wall under pure extension
solution: Reverse: shortening. Thrust: low angle (<45°). Nappes: large displacement thrusts.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: To which class of silicate structures does the mineral olivine belong?
options: Sorosilicates (paired SiO4 tetrahedra sharing an apex)
Inosilicates (chain structures of linked tetrahedra)
Nesosilicates (independent SiO4 tetrahedra)
Phyllosilicates (continuous sheets of SiO4 tetrahedra)
solution: Olivine (Mg,Fe)2SiO4 — high-T mineral. Mantle rock peridotite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: During the recovery phase of a pumping test, residual drawdown s' is given by which formula?
options: Recovery data yield the storage coefficient S but never the value of T
Residual drawdown s' = (2.303Q)/(4πT)·log(t/t'). No S estimate needed
Recovery analysis requires pumping at two different constant discharge rates
Residual drawdown is recorded only during the pumping phase of the test
solution: Recovery: T from slope of s' vs log(t/t'). More reliable than drawdown (constant rate).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Liptinite (exinite) macerals in coal are derived from which kinds of plant parts?
options: Woody plant tissue such as cellulose and lignin of tree stems
Oxidized or charred plant fragments and fungal remains
Mineral matter introduced into the coal during diagenesis
Waxy, resinous plant parts (spores, cuticles, algae, resins)
solution: Liptinite: sporinite, cutinite, alginite, resinite. High hydrogen, oil-prone.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: For fold axis determination, what does the β-axis on a stereonet represent, and what does a π-girdle of poles to bedding indicate?
options: The fold axis is found by plotting the strike directions and taking their average azimuth
The fold axis is simply the dip direction of the steepest limb measured in the field
The fold axis is determined from the plunge of the axial plane cleavage at the hinge zone
Beta (β) axis: intersection of two limbs. Pi (π) girdle: poles to bedding
solution: π-diagram: poles to bedding on girdle. β-axis: maximum density point on π-circle.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How is the refractive index of a mineral determined relative to its mounting medium?
options: Determined by Becke line method. Mineral vs mounting medium
Determined by comparing relief against the mounting medium
Determined by the mineral's interference color at extinction
Determined by optical dispersion in plane polarized light only
solution: Becke line: bright line moves into higher RI medium when stage is lowered.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In site investigation for a dam foundation, which borehole test directly measures the in-situ permeability of the rock mass?
options: Standard Penetration Test (SPT)
Lugeon (packer) test
Unconfined compressive strength test
Schmidt hammer rebound test
solution: Lugeon (packer) test: water is injected under pressure into an isolated borehole section; 1 Lugeon ≈ 1 L/min per metre at 10 bars ≈ 10⁻⁷ m/s. Used for grouting design.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The Darcy velocity of groundwater flow through a porous medium is defined as the:
options: Volumetric flow rate per unit cross-sectional area
Actual speed of a water particle moving through the pores
Total discharge divided by the effective porosity of the medium
Ratio of the hydraulic gradient to the hydraulic conductivity
solution: q = Q/A = Ki. Apparent velocity through total area.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the nature and tectonic setting of the Closepet Granite batholith in southern India?
options: Early Archean (3.4 Ga) supracrustal belt within the Sargur greenstone sequence
Granite batholith between E and W Dharwar Cratons. ~2.5 Ga. Late Archean
Proterozoic (~1.8 Ga) platform carbonate sequence of the Cuddapah basin
Paleozoic (Permian) coal-bearing rift fill of the Gondwana basins of India
solution: Closepet: N-S trending. High-K, calc-alkaline. Anatectic origin. Mantle+crustal source.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which mineral and depositional setting are characteristic of major phosphorite deposits?
options: Lacustrine deposits in rift lakes formed by evaporation of alkaline brines
Placer concentrations of heavy minerals along high-energy wave-dominated beaches
Francolite (carbonate fluorapatite). Upwelling zones. Peru-Chile, Morocco
Biogenic silica oozes from diatoms and radiolarians on the deep ocean floor
solution: Phosphorite: P₂O₅ > 18%. Important fertilizer source. Pelletal or nodular.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Crystal twinning: contact twin vs penetration twin:
options: No difference. Contact and penetration twins are simply two names for the same intergrowth
Contact = interpenetrating. The two types share identical geometry at the junction
Contact: shared plane (mirror). Penetration: shared point (interpenetrating)
Same thing. Both twins form by the same interpenetrating growth mechanism
solution: Contact: staurolite, gypsum. Penetration: fluorite, pyrite, garnet twins.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which Indian ore deposit is a world-class porphyry copper-molybdenum deposit hosted in granitoid rocks?
options: Malanjkhand, Madhya Pradesh
Kolar, Karnataka
Zawar, Rajasthan
Bailadila, Chhattisgarh
solution: Malanjkhand (Madhya Pradesh): porphyry Cu-Mo deposit. Kolar is a gold deposit, Zawar an MVT Pb-Zn deposit, and Bailadila an iron ore (BIF) deposit.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A symplectite is best described as what type of texture in metamorphic rocks?
options: Regular growth of a single mineral phase in optical continuity across a twin plane with no second phase present
Overgrowth of a new mineral in crystallographic continuity around an older detrital or igneous core
Intergrowth of two minerals (e.g., Cpx + Pl) replacing higher-P assemblage. Opx + Cpx + Pl from Grt breakdown
Exsolution of a second mineral phase from a homogeneous alkali-feldspar host during slow cooling
solution: Symplectite: vermicular texture. Decompression reaction. Fingerprint of rapid exhumation.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which desert landform is a crescent-shaped sand dune whose horns point downwind?
options: Barchan
Yardang
Inselberg
Playa
solution: Barchan: crescent-shaped dune with horns pointing downwind, formed on firm flat desert surfaces. Yardang is a wind-eroded ridge; playa is a desert lake basin.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Granite classification — S, I, A, M types:
options: Explosive volcanic classification of igneous rocks based on silica content and the explosivity index of their eruptions
Division restricted to granodiorite and tonalite on the basis of modal quartz
Classification based only on the colour index and grain size of the rock
S (sedimentary source, peraluminous), I (igneous source, metaluminous), A (anorogenic, alkaline), M (mantle)
solution: S-type: muscovite, monazite. I-type: hornblende, titanite. A-type: fluorite, high Ga/Al.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 35% volatile matter and 20% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+35+20) = 41%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer (K = 10 m/day) of cross-section 500 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The groundwater discharge is about:
options: 50 m³/day
100 m³/day
200 m³/day
5000 m³/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In coal petrography, the vitrinite reflectance value (approximately) marking the boundary between bituminous and anthracite rank is:
solution: Vitrinite reflectance (%Ro): ~0.5-1.0 = high-volatile bituminous, ~1.0-2.0 = medium/low-volatile bituminous, >2.0 = anthracite. Also used as a thermal maturity indicator for hydrocarbons.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A rock sample of 100 cm³ contains 15 cm³ of pore space. Its porosity is:
solution: Porosity = (void volume/total volume)×100 = 15/100 = 15%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In a thrust duplex, the displacement between the floor thrust and the roof thrust is transferred by which structures?
options: Horses bounded by imbricate thrusts that splay from the floor thrust and rejoin the roof thrust
A single normal fault cutting across both thrusts
Strike-slip tear faults oriented parallel to the transport direction
Conjugate shear joints developed in the hanging wall
solution: Duplex: a series of horses between a floor thrust and a roof thrust, each bounded by imbricate (horse-bounding) thrusts that branch off the floor and rejoin the roof, transferring displacement upward.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which texture, with elongated olivine blades, is characteristic of komatiites?
options: Spinifex texture (elongated olivine blades)
Interlocking granular texture formed by equal-size equant crystals of plagioclase
Porphyritic texture with large quartz and feldspar phenocrysts in a glassy base
Ophitic texture defined by plagioclase laths enclosed in pyroxene oikocrysts
solution: Komatiite: Archean ultramafic volcanic. Spinifex due to rapid cooling.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A rock retains 25% of its original parent isotope (half-life 4.47 Gyr). Its radiometric age is about:
options: 4.47 Gyr
8.94 Gyr
2.24 Gyr
solution: 25% remaining ⇒ 2 half-lives ⇒ age = 2×4.47 = 8.94 Gyr.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which remote sensing system uses an active sensor operating in the microwave region and can image at night as well as through cloud cover?
options: A passive sensor recording natural microwave emissions from the Earth surface
An optical sensor that is limited to daytime use and cloud-free conditions
Active sensor. Day/night, cloud penetration. SAR: synthetic aperture
A thermal sensor that measures emitted longwave radiation during the night
solution: Radar: transmits pulses. Backscatter depends on roughness, moisture, geometry. Interferometry.
